description: On June 14, 2011, around 10:30 p.m., two people were intrigued by the silent, variable-speed movements of a luminous object in the sky. The observation lasted between 5 and 10 minutes. On June 16, these two people returned to the site and discovered a circular area of flattened grass, 1.5 meters in diameter, amidst tall grass. The description of the phenomenon was twofold. First, a powerful white light, moving two to three times faster than an airplane, was described, accompanied by a red glow when the object passed through a cloud: this clearly corresponds to observations from the International Space Station (ISS). Second, a separate phenomenon, independent of the first, rapidly changing trajectory and speed, suggested a helicopter, but GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of Aeronautical and Space Explorations) was unable to verify this hypothesis, and the witness account was not precise enough to support this explanation. Of moderate strangeness, this observation would be classified as A for the first part, C for the second, and irrelevant for the tracks in the grass. Overall, this case is classified as C due to a lack of detailed information on the second part of the observation.

summary: Observing the passage of the International Space Station.
description: On June 13, 2011, after 11:00 PM, a witness observed a bright point of light moving rapidly across the sky from their home. This point followed a downward trajectory, dimmed, and then disappeared behind a cloud. No unusual noises were heard during this observation. The International Space Station's pass file and its ground track are consistent with the witness's observation. The ATV2 vehicle was docked at the station at that time, and the magnitude for this pass was -3.5, meaning it was very bright and visible to the naked eye. Since the witness did not see the beginning of the pass over the station's zenith, they interpreted the end of the pass as a descent. This case is classified as Class A, like the ISS observation.

summary: Probable observations of a luminous display in the sky.
description: motorist and his passengers observed the rapid and random movements of a luminous, oval-shaped object in the sky. Bluish in color, it moved across the cloud ceiling. Only one report was sent to GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information and Experimentation on Astronomy). The described characteristics (a blue luminous object "above" the clouds, the impression of "a large electric torch," random movements in direction and altitude, a 30-minute observation period, and the observation at 2:00 AM on a long, festive weekend) inevitably suggest the observation of a light show from one of the many nightclubs in the Agde-Béziers region. These types of moving objects on cloud ceilings are frequently misinterpreted, and depending on weather conditions, the beams may not be visible. Locating and precisely identifying the nightclub in question would add nothing to the already low degree of strangeness of an observation whose characteristics are mostly those of a known phenomenon. The case is classified as Class B, like the probable observation of a nightclub light show.

summary: Observation of the movement of a red light in the Tahitian sky: lack of information.
description: On June 12, 2011, at 6:36 PM, several people on the beach at Punaaiua Bay (Tahiti) observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. A very bright red light moved at high speed, then stopped and disappeared vertically into the night. Only one eyewitness account was reported, accompanied by photographs. Of moderate strangeness and good consistency, this case is reminiscent of a Thai lantern in many respects. However, due to the abrupt end of the phenomenon, this hypothesis is too tenuous to be accepted, as the local wind conditions cannot be known or modeled. This case is provisionally classified as Class C, pending further reports.

summary: Observations of the silent and rapid passage of a bright red-yellow luminous ball: probable observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.
description: On Sunday, June 12, 2011, at approximately 1:26 a.m., two witnesses were surprised to see a bright, yellow-red ball streak across the sky at high speed. No unusual noise was heard as the object moved in a straight line. The observation lasted about three minutes. While not particularly unusual, the observation was fairly consistent despite the lack of elevation data (likely due to confusion about its altitude). This case exhibits all the characteristics of a misidentification involving a Thai lantern. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable Thai lantern sighting.

summary: Observation of three objects rotating on their own axis in the sky: lack of information.
description: During a walk in the Corbières mountains on June 2, 2011, at 6:15 PM, a witness observed three white, metallic objects spinning rapidly above the Albas valley (Aude). The three objects disappeared into the clouds after one minute. While of moderate strangeness, the evidence is weak due to the imprecise location of the witness and the direction of movement of the observed phenomenon. Therefore, this case cannot be definitively concluded. It is classified as a C case due to a lack of independent and corroborating witness statements.

summary: Observation of numerous white dots in the sky at very high altitude: probable observation of balloons.
description: witness reported an observation made with binoculars on May 29, 2011, between 10:41 PM and 10:45 PM. He observed the slight, random east-south movement of about a hundred white points of light. Given the small, uncohesive movement of the group, which correlates with the light winds at the time, GEIPAN hypothesized that these white points were balloons released for a celebration, dimly illuminated by city lights (no moon visible at that time). GEIPAN classified this case as "B," indicating a probable observation of balloons.

summary: Observation of the movement of a white light: probable observation of an aircraft.
description: witness reported an observation made on May 25, 2011, at 2:09 AM: through a window, the witness observed a bright white light to the north. The phenomenon followed a straight trajectory southward before turning east-southeast. The observation lasted five seconds before the light suddenly disappeared. No noise was heard during the phenomenon. The leading hypothesis is that the observer was looking directly at an aircraft coming from the north, preparing to land at Orléans or Orly airport, with its landing lights illuminated. When the observer faced the aircraft, it appeared as a nearly stationary point (the flashing lights were not visible because the front landing lights were blinding), and its distance could not be estimated. These landing lights are visible from more than 10 km along their axis. If the aircraft changes course, the point of light moves laterally, changes brightness, and then appears and disappears because the observer is no longer directly in line with the searchlights. If the aircraft is not too far away, the flashing lights can then be seen. The phenomenon should recur from time to time when weather conditions are similar. The absence of noise is not surprising if we assume that the witness's distance estimation is incorrect, an estimation impossible to make at night based on a point of light. This case is class "B": probable sighting of an aircraft.

summary: A stain on a photograph without direct visual evidence during the shooting process.
description: A witness sent us a photograph showing an intriguing object in front of the aircraft being photographed. This witness did not make any direct observation when the photograph was taken. The blurred object against the sky is most likely an insect or a bird in flight, its blur and elongated shape caused by the animal's movement during the 1/100th of a second exposure. Furthermore, the witness noticed nothing at the time the photograph was taken, so this was not a direct observation.

summary: Probable observation of the movement of Thai lanterns.
description: A witness reported an observation made on May 21, 2011, at 1:55 a.m.: in the sky, a group of seven luminous red-orange orbs moved slowly in a south-north direction. No sound was heard during the observation before these lights disappeared behind the clouds. The description perfectly matches the classic description of Thai lanterns: color, brightness, number, and movement with the wind. The witness noted that Lille was celebrating double the sound in football that evening, which could have been an opportunity for a lantern release. This case is classified as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Prolonged observation from an airplane of a white sphere with very blurry edges.
description: person reported the following unexplained events: a passenger on a commercial airliner on May 21, 2011, witnessed the plane encountering turbulence under a clear blue sky with a layer of clouds below. The witness then observed a large, horizontal brown trail parallel to the aircraft and, below the wing, a white sphere about the size of a penny held at arm's length. He took photographs. The observation lasted approximately fifteen minutes, between 7:55 PM and 8:10 PM. The gray trail is the shadow cast by the aircraft's contrail on the cloud layer, and the bright sphere is an atmospheric optical phenomenon (similar to the Brocken spectrum): backscattering of light in mist droplets towards the observer, who was facing the sun. This explanation assumes that the vibrations felt by the witnesses were independent of this phenomenon. The disappearance of the bright ball is probably due to the interruption of the cloud layer.

summary: Probable observations of the movement of Thai lanterns.
description: On May 13, 2011, at 12:35 a.m., several people observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. One witness reported seeing seven very bright orange orbs moving. The witness's description matches the characteristics of Thai lanterns in terms of color, number, and altitude. The circular and erratic movements may seem surprising, but in urban areas, there are many sources of local atmospheric turbulence: car traffic, forced ventilation in buildings, and heating or air conditioning. Other reports indicate disordered movements of lanterns over cities. Even though the licking of Thai lanterns is prohibited in cities, it appears that this prohibition is not always respected, perhaps due to ignorance on the part of those responsible. This case is therefore classified as "B": probable Thai lanterns.

summary: Witness observation of a bright white point in the sky: lack of information.
description: On May 13, 2011, at approximately 11:30 PM, a witness observed a bright white point in the sky from his backyard, which intrigued him. During the observation, which lasted less than three minutes, the witness noted the object moving northwest without hearing any noise. No other reports of this phenomenon were received. The witness saw a very bright point, seemingly stationary for a few seconds, which then moved and diminished over a few seconds. One possible cause could be an airplane that, heading directly towards the witness, appeared stationary; its landing lights were then pointed in the witness's direction, resulting in maximum brightness. The airplane may have then changed course, causing the beam of the landing lights to move away from the witness's direction, which perceived it less and less; from the witness's perspective, the point moved laterally until it disappeared when the airplane's axis was too far from the direction of the airplane and the witness. Given the relatively minor nature of the phenomenon, GEIPAN did not investigate to identify the aircraft involved. Therefore, this case remains classified as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Regular observations of the movement of a point of light: probable observation of aircraft.
description: witness regularly observes a bright point of light moving across the sky from their home. This point grows larger and then smaller before disappearing over the horizon. The witness is almost directly in line with one of the runways at Orly Airport. With a northerly wind, planes take off directly in front of the witness. The aircraft's headlights are highly directional and very powerful; the witness cannot distinguish the flashing red lights, which are much less powerful. When the plane deviates from the observation path, the light received by the witness diminishes significantly. The repetitive nature of the observation supports this hypothesis; the witness could verify that this occurs with a northerly wind. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of planes taking off from Orly.

summary: Observation of the movement of a bright orange glow with changes of direction: probable observation of the movement of a Thai lantern.
description: witness reported an observation on April 29, 2011, at 9:50 PM: upon closing his bedroom shutters, he noticed a bright orange glow in the sky. The changes in direction intrigued the observer. The witness's description matches the appearance of a Thai lantern in a light wind within a fairly turbulent urban environment, which caused these sudden changes in direction. The color, brightness, and duration are consistent with a Thai lantern.

summary: Probable observation of pollen passage.
description: witness observed pollen drifting from nearby trees from their balcony. Suddenly, a bright point of light rapidly crossed the sky between two clouds. No sound was heard during the observation, and the point disappeared into the cloudy sky. The witness observed, during the day and almost directly into the sun, a white ball crossing the blue sky between two clouds. The witness noted that there was a large amount of pollen floating in the air. It was probably one of these cottony pollen grains (pollen or seeds?) that, when exposed to the sun, turned silvery. The movement in the direction of the wind (east wind of 15 to 31 km/h, the Autan wind) confirms this hypothesis. (For information, the investigator observed this phenomenon several times from their home in May on days with the Autan wind). This case is therefore classified as "B": probable observation of tree pollen or seeds (plane tree?).

summary: Observations of the silent movement of about ten luminous points.
description: On Thursday, April 21, 2011, several people observed waves of silent, luminous orange phenomena moving across the sky. The photos submitted were similar to those of many other cases involving sightings of Chinese lanterns. The swirling winds present that evening could explain the trajectory described by the witness. Even though no formal testimony has yet corroborated the release of lanterns, GEIPAN considers this hypothesis highly probable.

summary: Observation of the SW-NE movement of a white light: passage of the ISS.
description: On April 19, 2011, at 9:37 PM, two people observed, from the terrace of a house, the slow, straight passage of a luminous white sphere over the mountain ridge of the Risoux massif. The main witness filmed their observation. Unfortunately, the film quality did not allow the police to make a specific interpretation and did not accurately reflect the witness's observation (significant camera shake at maximum zoom and artifacts). The directions and times of the observation correspond exactly to a pass of the International Space Station (ISS): this case is classified as "A": perfectly identified.

summary: Observation of the very rapid movement of two parallel red points: lack of information.
description: On April 17, 2011, at 12:05 AM, a witness reported seeing two bright red dots, slightly offset in the sky, moving at a rapid and identical speed along an upward trajectory. No other reports were collected. The speed of the phenomena and the upward trajectory of the lights suggest a possible sighting of distress flares. The lack of information received prevents confirmation of this hypothesis and any further investigation.

summary: Observation of a black cylindrical object passing over the house: straight trajectory.
description: On April 17, 2011, at approximately 8:30 PM, a witness heard a muffled, turbine-like noise coming from the sky and saw an object moving at high speed in the air, passing very close to the roof ridge of his house in a straight line. The object was described as cylindrical, 80 cm long and 20 to 30 cm wide. It was black, and no odor or light was observed. The object moved away in the direction of the village. An investigation by a National Police Inspector (IPN) failed to find a coherent explanation, although the object resembled a drone, but of an unknown model. The witness repeatedly described to the Gendarmerie and the IPN, without altering his account, what could be considered a UFO (Unidentified Floating Object). This case is classified as D1: unidentified. However, it should be noted on the one hand that the case file is relatively weak: a single testimony, a very brief observation, without photos or videos, and on the other hand that the performance of the machine is not very different from known machines.

summary: Observations of the silent movement of lights in the sky.
description: Two witnesses reported observing the silent movement of lights over the ocean on Sunday, April 17, 2011, between 9:50 p.m. and 10:10 p.m. The description of the phenomenon is identical in every respect to that of Thai lanterns. The wind direction (East, Northeast) is consistent with the observed movement. It should simply be noted that the observation took place on a Sunday, which is not the usual day for lantern releases; however, it was during the school holidays.

summary: Probable sightings of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On April 16, 2011, at approximately 2:20 a.m., a driver and his passenger were intrigued by the horizontal movement of about ten luminous orange orbs. These moved silently from the northeast to the southwest before gradually disappearing. The witnesses' account (orange lights moving, extinguishing after a few minutes) and the wind direction (northeast) are entirely consistent with the observation of Thai lanterns. The day and time (late weekend evening) are also typical for a lantern release following a festival. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Probable observation of light animations made with a laser projector.
description: On April 14, 2011, at approximately 9:45 PM, a witness observed a light moving rapidly for a few minutes. It traced figure-eight patterns in the cloudy sky. The witness's description perfectly matches the appearance of laser projectors used for festive events (nightclubs, fairs, special events). The presence of low clouds made the phenomenon highly visible. It is worth noting that the funfair was taking place in Reims that day, which is likely the cause of the phenomenon.

summary: Observations of bright white lights seemingly emitted by a slowly moving object: lack of information.
description: On April 9, 2011, at approximately 10:45 PM, two witnesses in a car very quickly spotted white lights that appeared to be emitted by a dark object moving in the immediate vicinity of the roof of a neighboring house. The group of lights seemed close and moved very slowly, without any perceptible noise from inside the vehicle. The lights disappeared behind the roof. The witnesses got out of the car and tried to find it again, but in vain. Many hypotheses are compatible with this observation: airplanes, helicopters, Thai lanterns (although these are usually yellow, orange, or red). Only the atmospheric reentry of a meteor or space debris, as well as a satellite pass, can be ruled out. Due to its limited consistency and unusual nature, this observation cannot be definitively concluded. The Thai lantern hypothesis might be plausible if the witness had noted yellow or orange lights. This case is class C due to inaccuracies in the testimony.

summary: Observation of a child's balloon shaped like a horse passing by.
description: witness reported an observation on April 8, 2011, around 8:00 AM: for approximately three minutes, he observed an unusual object passing across a perfectly clear sky. The object's shape was quickly identified as a rearing horse. Photographs were taken. The witness provided the entire account, clearly identifying a large balloon representing Pegasus.

summary: Observation of a white light coming from an unrecognized and silent craft: lack of information.
description: On April 8, 2011, at approximately 11:30 PM, a witness in a car observed a bright light in the sky. He stopped, opened his window, and saw a huge object equipped with blinding white lights, hovering about 50 meters above a house. No sound was heard. The lights went out, and the object rotated before departing: the witness could then see that the object had a triangular shape. Due to the unusual nature of the case, GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) wanted to conduct a field investigation, but this was only requested in 2014. As the witness lives relatively far from the observation site and has limited availability, this interview could not be arranged. The more than three-year delay since the observation also seemed too long to the witness. Despite its high degree of strangeness, the consistency of this observation case is currently too weak to allow for a D classification for unexplained phenomena: a single, very brief testimony with many inaccuracies, written a year after the events. In the absence of additional data, GEIPAN classifies this case as C.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon changing from white to orange then to red: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On April 7, 2011, at 11:06 PM, a witness living on the 7th floor of a building observed a curious luminous phenomenon in the sky. The witness described it as a cluster of two closely spaced, roughly oval shapes that changed from white to orange, then turned red, and disappeared without any unusual sound. The observed phenomenon resembled two Thai lanterns moving away from the observer. The color change from white to orange and then to red, along with the movement in a direction close to the observer's line of sight, supports this hypothesis. It is possible that these lanterns were launched from the banks of the Seine not far from the observer and then followed the wind, roughly from north to south. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of a very bright bluish ball passing straight across the sky, changing color before disappearing: probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.
description: On April 5, 2011, at 5:21 a.m., a motorist noticed a light appearing in the sky. He described a very bright, bluish ball that rapidly crossed the sky in a straight line. The phenomenon then changed color to orange and seemed to stop before disappearing. The front passenger made the same observation. Only one witness statement was recorded. This case of low strangeness and low to medium consistency appears to have all the characteristics of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid. However, a Class A classification is ruled out in the absence of independent sources. This case is classified as Class B, as a probable bolide: atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.

summary: Observation of the passage of luminous balls: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: Several people reported seeing, around 11 p.m. on April 2, 2011, a group of numerous orange orbs moving silently across the sky above the city; these orbs then disappeared instantly. The witnesses' descriptions perfectly match those of Thai lanterns (orange lights that drift with the wind and last less than 20 minutes). Another lecher occurred a week later (see the article in the L'Est Républicain newspaper of April 11, 2011, in the official report). This case is therefore classified as "B"; identification is highly probable, but the perpetrators of the lecher have not been found.

summary: Probable observation of an Iridium flare.
description: A witness reported a very brief observation of a very bright white ball that appeared to be coming towards them and then disappearing as it rose back up into the sky. No unusual noise was heard. No other reports were collected. The description of the phenomenon suggests a reflection of the sun off an Iridium satellite (see /index.php?id=299). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of an Iridium flare.

summary: Observation of a red ball with sudden disappearance: probable observation of the front spotlight of an aircraft seen from the front.
description: On March 23, 2011, at approximately 11:30 PM, a motorist noticed a large, reddish-colored sphere in the sky. He stopped and photographed it just before it suddenly disappeared. The witness's description corresponds to a head-on observation of an aircraft approaching from the east (perhaps the Nice-Toulouse flight that landed at Blagnac Airport around 9:55 PM): facing the aircraft, the observer saw the aircraft's nose landing light as a stationary point (the flashing lights were not visible because the nose light was blinding). If the aircraft changed course slightly, for example, to align with the Blagnac runway centerline, the point of light moved laterally and then disappeared because the witness was no longer directly in front of the landing lights. This is the hypothesis accepted by GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Specialized Operations Group), classifying this case as "B": probable head-on observation of an aircraft.

summary: Probable observation of a meteorite passing by.
description: On March 21, 2011, at 5:03 a.m., a witness observed a silent, yellow-orange trail passing for a few seconds along a descending E-NE trajectory. This person likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry: the description of the phenomenon perfectly matches the appearance of a meteorite impact.

summary: pilot's evasive maneuver after seeing a faceted, spherical object.
description: On Sunday, March 20, 2011, at 3:30 PM, a witness piloting an aircraft, which was slightly above the Dreux airfield, evaded an object shaped like a polygon with numerous black and some green facets. This object, estimated to be between 2 and 3 meters in diameter, appeared to be stationary or moving very slowly. By the time the pilot had turned around, the object had disappeared. The object encountered was probably a thermal balloon (or solar balloon), launched by amateurs. The black color, the apparent absence of a gondola, and the size are consistent with this hypothesis. We have not found any other examples of thermal balloons of this shape. The balloon's disappearance could possibly be explained by turbulence caused by the aircraft, which destabilized it and caused it to descend rapidly. The case is classified as Class B in the associated investigation report.

summary: Observation through binoculars of two triangular shapes with flashing lights.
description: On Sunday, March 20, 2011, between 9:45 p.m. and 10:00 p.m., several members of the same family were observing the sky and were intrigued by the presence of two particularly bright and moving stars. One of the witnesses then observed, through binoculars, two triangular shapes with flashing orange lights. The two objects moved at a constant speed across the sky, following a straight trajectory from north to east. No noise was heard during the observation. No other reports were filed regarding this phenomenon. The police investigation focused on the theory of an in-flight refueling operation by military aircraft that had been operating in the area described by the witness.

summary: Observation of the movement of a light: astronomical observation of the star Deneb.
description: On March 20, 2011, at approximately 8:30 PM, a driver observed a light in the sky that intrigued and frightened her. The object observed by the witness turned out to be always in the same direction. As it was very distant, it appeared to follow the observer. The vertical movements were an illusion, perceived relative to the horizon, which naturally varies along the route. The change in color of a point of light on the horizon is due to atmospheric turbulence. The direction indicated by the witness, to the left of her E/NE direction, was actually N/NE. At that point in the sky, the star Deneb, one of the brightest stars in the sky (one of the three in the Summer Triangle), was shining. This case is classified as "A": Confusion with the star Deneb.

summary: Successive observations of Venus.
description: witness observed and filmed multiple sightings of a white light in the sky (February 9, March 6 and 11, 2011). The characteristics of the observation described by the witness (phenomenon observed "several mornings upon waking," "white in color," disappearing when it was light, observation of a stationary phenomenon for a very long period of 45 minutes...) suggest an astronomical phenomenon. Verification of the observation direction towards the south-southeast (Lavelanet-Belesta direction) and the astronomical configuration of the sky on those days, and particularly on March 11, 2011, around 7:00 a.m. local time, leaves no doubt that the planet Venus was present in the observed area of the sky and clearly visible to the naked eye. The classic twinkling effect described by the witness is due to atmospheric disturbances (differences in temperature and refractive index of the layers traversed). The case is class A, like the observation of the planet Venus.

summary: Probable sightings of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On March 6, 2011, at approximately 10:15 PM, two witnesses observed several luminous red-orange objects passing in a straight line across the sky, appearing at intervals. No noise was heard during the observation, which was filmed. Photographs were also taken. The description of the phenomenon suggested the passage of Thai lanterns. The videos provided by the witness show the passage of a red-orange object very similar to other videos reported to GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information and Experimentation on Astronomy) that definitively show the passage of Chinese lanterns. This possibility was not ruled out by the witness himself (letter dated March 25, 2011), and after examining all the evidence, GEIPAN's hypothesis is that the observation was likely that of the passage of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of complex movements of a white luminous object: lack of information.
description: On February 26, 2011, at 7:45 PM, a witness was intrigued by the presence of a very bright white object in the sky. This object was moving along an east-west axis, but with both upward and downward movements. The observation lasted three minutes before the object, on its descending trajectory, disappeared into the night sky. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon. The observed phenomenon presents a certain degree of strangeness due to the complex movements of the observed point. The hypothesis of a helicopter or a military aircraft can be considered, but GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) processed this case too late to be able to verify it. Due to a lack of information and the unique nature of this witness report, this case is classified as "C".

summary: Probable sighting of a flying lantern.
description: witness reports an observation made with their family on February 26, 2011, around 9:45 PM: they all observed the movement of a luminous orange ball with a sudden change of direction and disappearance in an upward trajectory at a "lightning" speed. This observation presents a low degree of strangeness insofar as a large proportion of the described characteristics correspond to those of known phenomena very often observed and reported to GEIPAN: observation of a luminous flying lantern (see the investigation report).

summary: Probable observations of discotheque light beams.
description: witness reported observing, at precisely 11:00 PM on February 26, 2011, halos of white light in an ovoid shape. The police investigation corroborated this testimony with those of other individuals. These observations, precise regarding the location, led the police to conclude that the halos were beams of light used that evening by a local nightclub.

summary: Probable observation of a meteor passing by.
description: On February 20, 2011, at 9:05 PM, a motorist observed a bright green, fluorescent glow moving across the sky, splitting into three spheres, and then disappearing. The observation resembled a fairly typical meteor: green light, straight trajectory, trail, and a duration of a few seconds. However, the fragmentation was not systematic. The object causing this phenomenon could have been a small piece of satellite debris, but it was more likely of natural origin (a meteorite).

summary: Multiple observations of a fireball rapidly passing on a downward trajectory in the sky: probable observations of atmospheric reentry.
description: GEIPAN has received several reports of a luminous phenomenon rapidly passing across the sky. The observations were made in Peypin (13), on the RN 568 between Arles and Fos-sur-Mer (13), and from a helicopter flying over a resort in the Pyrénées 2000 area (the numbers 91 and 93 in the case name refer to the region code). The descriptions combine the characteristics (shape, trajectory, rapid angular movement) of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid or space debris. Furthermore, the similarity, based on the appearance, the general north-south direction, and especially the time, with other reports (outside of GEIPAN) from fairly distant locations, strongly suggests that this atmospheric reentry was visible to distant witnesses because it occurred at a high altitude (50 to 150 km). See the article on canalblog. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable atmospheric reentry.

summary: Motorist observing for a few seconds a static, rather flat, triangular object with rounded corners.
description: On February 15, 2011, a motorist observed an object she did not recognize. She described it as a stationary object, triangular in shape with three rounded corners, rather flat, and greenish in color (between gray and green). Continuing on her way, the observation lasted only a few seconds. No other witness accounts of this phenomenon were reported. The witness, contacted by telephone, regularly drove through that area and had never seen anything like it. The witness's account is relatively precise, but it is surprising that there were no other reports, making it a strange, albeit inconsistent, case, as it was a single testimony without any recording (photo, video). The object described, hovering, did not resemble any known object, except perhaps a kite or hang glider, which would have been incongruous in that location.

summary: motorist observed a luminous ball moving close to the horizon with color changes: observation of Venus.
description: On Sunday, February 13, 2011, at 6:07 a.m., a motorist driving on the D940 between Lamarque-Pontarcq (65) and Lourdes (65) was intrigued by the slow movement of an orange sphere close to the horizon. The witness noticed an irregular brightness. Upon arriving home, he used his camera's zoom to continue his observation. This lasted approximately thirty minutes. Only one witness account was collected. Calculation of the observation directions shows that, based on the profile of the road taken by the witness (see map diagrams 1 and 2), the observation direction of the phenomenon is always roughly the same, on the order of 130° azimuth. Astronomical verification shows that the planet Venus is visible in this direction, extremely bright. This confusion is common: because the planet is low on the horizon, witnesses perceive it as close, flying over the landscape. The changes in color and detail are the result of atmospheric glare; these effects are very strong and variable near the horizon (similar to sunset). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the planet Venus.

summary: Observation in the sky of the rapid movement of a white light with a change of direction: probable International Space Station.
description: On February 3, 2011, between 7:20 and 7:24 AM, a witness in a parking lot observed a non-flashing white light moving quickly and straight across the sky, changing direction. No noise was heard during the observation, and no trail was seen. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected by the gendarmerie. This sighting was initially classified as D1 in 2011 by GEIPAN (the French UFO research group), then re-examined in 2013 with a new hypothesis proposed by an internet user. This case is of moderate consistency (only one eyewitness, no recording), but the description of the observed UFO is very precise. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color, trajectory) with a well-known astronautical object: the International Space Station (ISS), which was clearly visible in the observed area of the sky, even though the witness did not mention it. In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as UAP B, probable observation from the International Space Station.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On February 2, 2011, starting at 6:15 a.m., two witnesses observed a dark circle from their apartment living room, within which bright lights twinkled. About the size of a full moon, this phenomenon remained stationary for approximately fifteen minutes, then diminished and moved away, becoming a very bright point within seconds. The observation ended at 6:45 a.m. The initial hypothesis considered was that it was an astronomical observation of the planet Venus, particularly visible at this time of year (magnitude -3.9, therefore very bright) in the southeast (135th star) at 10 arcseconds above the horizon (see star chart). However, this hypothesis does not explain the observation of a dark circle and the bright lights, nor the speed at which the object disappeared. No other accounts of this phenomenon have been collected. Due to the nature of the observed phenomenon, a thorough investigation is difficult to conduct. The case is classified as "C" due to lack of information.

summary: Retrospective observation of round, grey patches on a photograph.
description: person takes photographs of a rainbow and the next day notices three unexplained, gray, spherical teche's in one of the photographs. Without direct observation during the shooting process, it is very difficult to explain the nature of teche's appearance in photos. The small black dot(s) cannot be explained by insect(s) flying close to the lens: the spherical shape and the season (winter) are inconsistent. The luminance of the main "object" is comparable to that of the electrical wire, indicating that the distance between the object and the lens was probably similar to the distance between the electrical wires and the camera lens. The most plausible explanation is the presence of balloons: small helium-filled balloons that may have moved or drifted away into the clouds before the next photograph was taken. Due to the lack of direct observation, no research has been conducted on the origin of these balloons.

summary: Observation of successive appearances of orange luminous phenomena in the sky: lack of information.
description: On Sunday, January 9, 2011, at approximately 6:50 PM, a witness observed several orange lights at low altitude. These lights appeared successively and moved silently and slowly across the sky. The witness filmed the observation as soon as the third UFO appeared. No other reports were collected. The description of the phenomenon strongly resembled successive appearances of Thai lanterns (color, speed of movement, low altitude, successive appearances from the same location). However, in this sparsely populated area, the origin and location of the lecher could not be determined through local investigations, and some elements appeared contradictory (passage behind clouds despite the object flying quite low). The possibility of images from a laser projector was also considered, but no beam was seen or filmed. Given all these uncertainties, GEIPAN classified this case as "C".

summary: Long filmed observation of a spherical, bright and stationary object, then observation of the presence of objects on the film without direct observation during filming.
description: On January 9, 2011, at 6:50 a.m., two people observed and filmed a bright, stationary, spherical object directly above an airfield. No unusual noises were heard during the observation. Upon reviewing the footage, other objects were noted, even though they had not been directly observed during the filming. Two phenomena are described in this testimony (see the investigation report): first, a bright, metallic-colored, spherical object, described as a scientific balloon (it was not a Météo-France balloon). Second, dark objects moving at high speed across the camera's field of view: these were likely flying insects about one meter from the camera.
